people.paul.role: Apostle who defends his message to the Galatians
people.paul.relations: He writes with all the brothers with him. He names Peter, Barnabas, and Titus in his story.
people.paul.meaning: Paul says he got his message by revelation, not from men. He tells how he met Peter and the other apostles. He opposes Peter at Antioch over the shared meal. He then tells the Galatians not to take on circumcision. He ends in his own hand.
people.jesus.role: Crucified and risen Lord who frees believers
people.jesus.relations: Paul says Jesus gave himself for our sins and God raised him. Paul calls believers children of God in Christ.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says his message came by revelation of Jesus Christ. He says Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law. He says all who are baptized into Christ are one. Paul says that in Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts.
people.peter.role: Apostle Paul visited, then opposed at Antioch
people.peter.relations: Paul calls him Cephas in 2:9. Paul stayed with him fifteen days. Barnabas joined his withdrawal.
people.peter.meaning: Paul visits Peter for fifteen days in Jerusalem. At Antioch Peter eats with the Gentiles. When people come from James, he draws back and separates himself. Paul says they did not walk uprightly. He confronts Peter before them all.
people.barnabas.role: Paul’s companion, carried away at Antioch
people.barnabas.relations: He goes up to Jerusalem with Paul and Titus. James, Cephas, and John gave him and Paul the right hand.
people.barnabas.meaning: Barnabas goes with Paul and Titus to Jerusalem. James, Cephas, and John give him and Paul the right hand of fellowship. At Antioch Paul says even Barnabas was carried away by the hypocrisy.
people.titus.role: Greek who went with Paul and was not circumcised
people.titus.relations: He goes up to Jerusalem with Paul and Barnabas.
people.titus.meaning: Paul takes Titus with him to Jerusalem. Titus is a Greek. Paul says he was not compelled to be circumcised. Paul says false brothers came in to spy on their liberty.
people.abraham.role: Ancestor who believed God and received a promise
people.abraham.relations: He had two sons, one by the servant and one by the free woman.
people.abraham.meaning: Paul says Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness. Paul says those of faith are his children. The promise came before the law, which came 430 years after. Paul says the law does not cancel it.
people.hagar.role: Abraham’s servant, used as a picture of bondage
people.hagar.relations: Paul says her son was born by the servant. He sets him beside the son of the free woman.
people.hagar.meaning: Paul calls the two women two covenants. He says Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia. He says she bears children to bondage. He says she answers to the Jerusalem that exists now. The letter does not give her own words.
people.isaac.role: Son of promise, born to the free woman
people.isaac.relations: Paul says the readers are children of promise as Isaac was. He is the son of the free woman.
people.isaac.meaning: Paul says Isaac was born through promise. Paul says the readers are children of promise like him. Paul says the one born by the flesh persecuted the one born by the Spirit. Paul says it is so now.
places.jerusalem.summary: Paul went up to Jerusalem to visit Peter in chapter 1. He went again with Barnabas and Titus in chapter 2. In chapter 4 he sets the Jerusalem that exists now beside the Jerusalem above.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The Jerusalem above has no map point.
places.damascus.summary: After he went into Arabia, Paul says he returned to Damascus (chapter 1).
places.damascus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.antioch-syria.summary: Paul says Peter came to Antioch in chapter 2. Peter ate with Gentiles there, then drew back. Paul opposed him to his face.
places.antioch-syria.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: All six chapters are the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: Paul’s accounts of his disputes are his own view. The guide did not check manuscripts, exact dates, or who his opponents were. It did not check the Greek words or any match with Acts. Hagar and Jerusalem are part of Paul’s own comparison. They are not an independent description of Jewish belief.
sources.works-galatians.summary: Works reads shared belonging through Christ alongside continuing difference.
sources.works-galatians.limits: This is Works’ own reading. The guide did not check her wider history of household guardians or baptism. It did not check her history of slavery or the later church. It did not review the linked commentaries and podcasts.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-40.summary: The lesson studies freedom, the fruit of the Spirit, and patient work.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-40.limits: Coverage follows the chapters the lesson discusses. The lesson does not review chapter two on its own. The guide read the Hinckley and Soares passages as quoted there. It did not read their full original works.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This Church-published atlas names towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: It supplies only the chosen reference coordinates. The earlier review record is unchanged. This source does not confirm Gospel events or exact routes.
sources.net-acts-map.summary: Opening descriptions and coordinates mark the cities named in Acts.
sources.net-acts-map.limits: These broad points do not confirm ancient events, travel paths, buildings, or coastlines. The guide did not adopt older encyclopedia claims about authorship, law, population, or exact dates.
chapters.*.mapNote: Markers show the cities Paul names in his memories. Mount Sinai and the Jerusalem above have no point.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: Paul’s remembered visits give no exact route and no full list of trips.
